headline: Highest risk is medium: Notion AI can ingest shared workspace content while ComfyUI is offline-only, creating default data-leakage and workflow-conflict paths; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented, but Notion AI can read workspace pages and ComfyUI can operate on files/models, so a manual copy-paste or shared-page bridge is plausible. Because both profiles lack a shared channel by default and ComfyUI is offline-only, the pathway is limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF the operator copies Notion AI output into a ComfyUI prompt or workflow note
IF a shared workspace page is used as an instruction carrier between the agents
mitigations: Keep prompts and outputs in separate pages
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from pasted text
Review copied text for imperative language before reuse
Disable any manual handoff workflow that reuses AI-generated prose

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and grounded in workspace content, while ComfyUI touches local models and workflows offline. If the same workspace contains sensitive material and operators move that content into ComfyUI prompts or assets, leakage can occur in default workflows. The pair does not prove exfiltration, but the shared-data path exists.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are copied into ComfyUI prompts, captions, or workflow metadata
IF the operator stores secrets in pages accessible to Notion AI and then exports them into image-generation assets
mitigations: Do not paste secrets into shared pages
Use a redaction step before exporting text to ComfyUI
Restrict workspace pages used for AI to non-sensitive content
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive projects into different workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have no filesystem write, no shell, and no git modification, so direct destructive write conflicts are blocked. The remaining overlap is limited to Notion workspace pages versus ComfyUI local model/workflow files, which is a narrow coordination issue rather than a strong concurrent-write hazard.
conditions: IF the operator manually mirrors the same artifact into both a Notion page and a ComfyUI workflow file
IF multiple Notion AI sessions edit the same workspace page while ComfyUI references exported copies
mitigations: Use one source of truth for each artifact
Avoid editing exported workflow text in Notion
Lock the handoff order: edit in one system, then export once
Name exported files with timestamps to reduce overwrite mistakes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is explicitly a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative summaries. If those summaries are then reused to drive ComfyUI prompts or workflow decisions, errors can cascade from Notion into generated assets. ComfyUI does not verify upstream claims by itself.
conditions: IF Notion AI summaries are copied into ComfyUI prompts without human verification
IF generated captions or instructions from Notion are used as authoritative workflow inputs
mitigations: Verify Notion summaries against source pages before reuse
Require a human review step before exporting text to ComfyUI
Mark AI-generated notes as untrusted in the workspace
Keep source citations alongside any copied summary

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and processes workspace content through Notion-controlled backends, while ComfyUI is offline and local. If regulated content is placed in Notion and then moved into ComfyUI assets or prompts, residency and retention expectations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific legal mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion workspace pages used by Notion AI
IF the operator exports that regulated content into ComfyUI prompts or generated files
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI workspaces
Use a policy checklist before copying content between tools
Document which data classes may enter each system
Delete temporary exports after use
